# OpenPDF Studio

> OpenPDF Studio is a local-first, open-source PDF workspace. The web/PWA version reads, annotates, edits, signs, OCRs, redacts, compresses and protects PDFs entirely in the browser. A separate native Windows desktop app (Rust + PDFium) provides local viewing, search, annotations and page extraction. Neither version uploads documents to a server.

Canonical: https://claudiobzrr.github.io/open-pdf-studio/

License: MIT

## Key facts

- Category: PDF reader, editor and privacy-first document workspace.
- Platform: web browser and installable PWA; native Windows 10/11 x64 desktop app (v0.2.0); offline after first load.
- Data handling: 100% local. No upload, account, telemetry or document backend.
- Web stack: React, TypeScript, PDF.js, pdf-lib (@cantoo), Tesseract.js, WebAssembly, Service Worker.
- Desktop stack: Rust, egui/eframe, PDFium, IBM Plex Sans. No webview, no Tauri.
- Web core features: rendering, text selection, search, annotations, page organization, AcroForm filling, local OCR with searchable PDF, AES-256 password protection, irreversible rasterized redaction, compression, visual comparison.
- Desktop 0.2.0 features: native rendering, tabs, thumbnails, search, zoom, view rotation, page extraction, rectangle annotations, sticky notes, Save/Save As, English/Portuguese UI.
- Desktop roadmap: OCR, AES-256, redaction, compression, comparison, certified signatures, forms and full page organization.
- Languages: English and Brazilian Portuguese.
- Limitations: no certified PAdES/ICP-Brasil signature, PDF/A preflight, XFA, 3D/multimedia, Adobe DRM or Document Cloud.
- Independence: not affiliated with Adobe; no proprietary Acrobat code and no license/DRM bypass.

## Best answers

- What is OpenPDF Studio? A private, open-source PDF workspace available in the browser and as a native Rust Windows desktop app.
- Is it free? Yes, MIT licensed with no paid tier.
- Do PDFs leave the device? No. Processing happens locally in browser memory or inside the native app.
- Does it work offline? Yes. The web app is a PWA; the desktop app is a local executable. OCR models are cached after first use in the web app.
- Is there a native desktop app? Yes. OpenPDF Studio Desktop 0.2.0 is built from scratch in Rust with egui and PDFium, not a Tauri/webview wrapper. It is a native viewer and annotator; heavier workflows remain on its roadmap.
- Can it replace Adobe Acrobat? It covers the everyday workflow with open-source equivalents, but not Adobe-specific certified signatures, PDF/A, XFA, DRM or cloud services.
